short: Sorting stock into A, B and C classes by value contribution.
seoTitle: ABC Analysis — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Sorting stock into A, B and C classes by value contribution. Attention is finite. See the formula, an example and the free Setu tools that use ABC Analysis.
definition: ABC analysis sorts inventory into three classes by annual consumption value: a small group of A items that account for most of the value, a middle B group, and a long tail of C items worth little individually.
bodyHtml:
Why ABC Analysis matters

Attention is finite. ABC analysis says where to spend it — tight counting and negotiation on A items, light-touch rules on C items — instead of treating every SKU as equally important.

ABC Analysis formula

Annual consumption value = Annual units used × Unit cost

Rank descending and take the cumulative share to draw the class boundaries.

How ABC Analysis works in practice

Rank items by annual usage value, take the cumulative percentage, and cut at roughly 70–80% for A and the next 15–20% for B. Set counting frequency, safety stock and review cadence by class.

faq.question: How often should ABC classes be refreshed?
faq.answer: Twice a year is usually enough, unless the range changes substantially.

faq.question: Should C items be dropped?
faq.answer: Not automatically. Some are low value but essential, which is why class is a guide to attention rather than to range.
